literal: Again the Nanjing Forbidden Army attacked Yang Tuan City, and the defending general surrendered the city.
idiomatic: The Nanjing Forbidden Army again attacked Yang Tuan City, and the garrison commander surrendered the city.

literal: An edict forbade raiding and plunder.
On jiyou day he encamped at Shenyu Village; an edict ordered reports submitted on the amounts of grain and armor and weapons at Yang Tuan City.
idiomatic: On jiyou day the court encamped at Shenyu Village and ordered reports on the grain and arms at Yang Tuan City.

literal: On xinhai day Heaven and Earth were sacrificed to with black and white victims.
idiomatic: On xinhai day the court sacrificed to Heaven and Earth with black and white victims.

literal: On guichou day Fengmu Garrison was taken and captive plunder was greatly permitted.
idiomatic: On guichou day the army took Fengmu Garrison and permitted extensive looting and the taking of captives.

literal: On bingchen day Xing Prefecture surrendered.
idiomatic: On bingchen day Xing Prefecture submitted.

literal: On dingsi day Shen Prefecture was taken; because it did not surrender immediately, the defending general and those below him were executed and the troops were allowed to plunder greatly.
idiomatic: On dingsi day the army stormed Shen Prefecture; because it did not surrender at once, the garrison commander and his subordinates were executed and the troops were turned loose to plunder.

literal: Li Jiqian led five hundred horsemen to pay respects at the border, wished to marry into the great state, and forever serve as a frontier vassal.
idiomatic: Li Jiqian came to the frontier with five hundred horsemen to submit, asked for a marriage alliance with the court, and pledged to serve forever as a border vassal.

literal: An edict enfeoffed Ting, daughter of Prince's Tent Military Commissioner Yelü Xiang, as Princess Yicheng and gave her in marriage below, granting three thousand horses.
idiomatic: An edict enfeoffed Ting, daughter of Prince's Tent military commissioner Yelü Xiang, as Princess Yicheng and gave her in marriage to him, with a grant of three thousand horses.
